In [[analytic number theory]], the '''Burgess inequality''' (also called the '''Burgess bound''') is an [[Inequality (mathematics)|inequality]]  that provides an [[upper bound]] for [[character sum]]s  
:<math>S_{\chi}(N,H):=\sum\limits_{N+1\leq n\leq N+H} \chi(n)</math>  
where <math>\chi</math> is a [[Dirichlet character]] modulo a cube free <math>q\in\mathbb{N}</math> that is not the [[Dirichlet character|principal character]] <math>\chi_0</math>.  

The inequality was proven in 1963 along with a series of related inequalities, by the [[United Kingdom|British]] mathematician [[David Allan Burgess]].<ref name="Burgess1963">{{cite journal |first=David A. |last=Burgess |title=On character sums and L-series, II |journal=Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society |volume=s3-13 |issue=1 |year=1963 |pages=524–536 |doi=10.1112/plms/s3-13.1.524}}</ref> It provides a better estimate for small character sums than the [[Pólya–Vinogradov inequality]] from 1918. More recent results have led to refinements and generalizations of the Burgess bound.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kerr |first1=Bryce | last2=Shparlinski |first2=Igor E. | last3=Yau | first3=Kam Hung |title=A Refinement of the Burgess Bound for Character Sums |journal=[[Michigan Mathematical Journal]] |doi=10.1307/mmj/1573700737 |doi-access=free |volume=69 |issue=2 |pages=227-240 |year=2020|arxiv=1711.10582 }}</ref>

== Burgess inequality ==
A number is called ''cube free'' if it is not divisible by any cubic number <math>x^3</math> except <math>\pm 1</math>. Define <math>r\in \mathbb{N}</math> with <math>r\geq 2</math> and <math>\varepsilon>0</math>.  

Let <math>\chi</math> be a Dirichlet character modulo <math>q\in\mathbb{N}</math> that is not a principal character. For two <math>N,H\in\mathbb{N}</math>, define the character sum  
:<math>S_{\chi}(N,H):=\sum\limits_{N+1\leq n\leq N+H} \chi(n).</math>  

If either <math>q</math> is cube free or <math>r\leq 3</math>, then the '''Burgess inequality''' holds<ref name="Burgess1963"/><ref>{{cite journal |title=An investigation into explicit versions of Burgess' bound |journal=Journal of Number Theory |volume=228 |pages=87–107 |year=2021 |doi=10.1016/j.jnt.2021.03.018 |doi-access=free |last1=Francis |first1=Forrest J.}}</ref>  
:<math>|S_{\chi}(N,H)|\leq C_{r,\varepsilon} H^{1-1/r}q^{(r+1)/(4r^2)+\varepsilon}</math>  
for some constant <math>C_{r,\varepsilon}</math>.

== References ==
* [[Henryk Iwaniec]] and [[Emmanuel Kowalski]], ''Analytic Number Theory'', American Mathematical Society Colloquium Publications, vol. 53, American Mathematical Society, Providence, RI, 2004.
